title: Generative AI
hook: The AI behind ChatGPT and image generators doesn't look up answers — it predicts what plausibly comes next, one piece at a time, until it has built a whole response.
key_points: Generative AI creates new content: text, images, audio, code — not just labels or scores.
Text models work by repeatedly predicting the next word from everything so far.
It generates what's *plausible*, which is why it can sound right while being wrong.
The same predict-the-next-piece trick powers writing, pictures, voices, and music.
content_html: Most older AI sorts things — is this spam or not, is this a cat or a dog. Generative AI makes things: a paragraph, a picture, a song, a snippet of code. It's the breakthrough behind ChatGPT and image tools, and the reason AI suddenly feels creative. Under the hood, a text generator is doing something almost surprisingly simple: predicting the next word, then the next, then the next, each time using everything written so far as the clue.
extra_html: Because it learned from an enormous amount of human writing, those next-word guesses string together into fluent, often genuinely useful answers. But notice what it's optimizing for: what sounds plausible, not what's true. The model has no fact-checker inside it. That single insight explains both the magic and the pitfalls — it can draft an email or explain a topic beautifully, and it can also state a confident "fact" that's completely invented. Image, audio, and video generators use the same core idea of building output piece by piece, which is why one technology now touches everything from customer-service bots to movie effects.

related.title: What AI Actually Is
related.hook: AI isn't a thinking robot — it's software that learns patterns from huge piles of examples, then uses them to make a good guess about something new.

related.title: Chatbots & Assistants
related.hook: ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini feel like talking to a person, but they're generative AI with a chat wrapper — brilliant writing partners, unreliable encyclopedias.

related.title: AI Images, Art & Video
related.hook: Type a sentence, get a picture. Image generators learned the link between words and visuals from billions of captioned images — which is also why artists are raising hard questions.

related.title: When AI Makes Things Up
related.hook: AI 'hallucinations' aren't glitches — they're the technology working as designed. A model that always predicts a plausible next word will sometimes produce a plausible falsehood.

related.title: How a Language Model Works
related.hook: A chatbot isn't reading and thinking — it's running the world's most sophisticated autocomplete, picking each next word from probabilities learned across billions of sentences.

flashcards.prompt: How does a text generator like ChatGPT produce an answer?

choices.text: By predicting the next word repeatedly, using everything written so far
By looking the answer up in a fact database
By copying the closest matching web page

flashcards.explanation_html: A text generator builds its reply one word at a time, each guess based on all the text so far — it isn't retrieving stored answers.

flashcards.prompt: Why can generative AI sound right but still be wrong?
flashcards.back_html: It's built to produce what's plausible, not what's true — there's no fact-checker inside it.
